---
title: "Introduction"
---
# Project Description
This project investigates the systemic migration of Nigerian healthcare talent, including doctors, nurses, and allied health professionals to the United Kingdom. Nigeria is facing an acute healthcare workforce crisis, characterized by a doctor-to-patient ratio of 1:9,083 and significant nursing shortages that threaten the sustainability of its healthcare system.

## The "Push" and the "Pull"
We frame this movement through two lenses: Nigeria's macro-economic pressures, i.e. inflation and unemployment; and UK's active recruitment to fill its own critical nursing and medical vacancies. We aim to determine if UK policy interventions, such as the 2021 Health and Care Worker Visa, act as a "vacuum" for Nigerian talent.

## Research Question
To what extent do macroeconomic conditions in Nigeria and immigration policy interventions in the UK influence the volume, geographic distribution, and professional deployment of Nigerian healthcare workers in the UK?


# Data Sources
To audit the movement of human capital, we are utilzing:

## Policy and Migration Flow
We combine annual migration data from the OECD International Migration Database (IMD) with qualitative policy data from the DEMIG POLICY Database.

## Labor Market and Spatial Distribution
We utilize granular UK Census data from ONS Nomis, cross-referenced with Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) codes to detect "Brain Waste" (skill mismatches).

## Economic Impact
Financial benchmarks are sourced from World Bank KNOMAD (remittances) and the IAB Brain Drain dataset to weigh human capital loss against financial gain.


# Sections
Our analysis is organized into three distinct sections:

## Policy and Flow
Analyzes whether migration "pulses" correlate more with UK policy shocks or Nigerian economic instability.

## Brain Waste and Spatial Distribution
Investigates career stagnation, mapping where Nigerian talent is concentrated in the UK and if they are stuck in roles below their qualification levels.

## The Economic vs. Human Capital Loss_
Quantifies the "Net Gain" for Nigeria, determining if remittance inflows truly compensate for the 1:9,083 healthcare crisis.
